title: Borrowing Arrows with Straw Boats
text:
In the novel Romance of the Three Kingdoms, the allied armies of Liu Bei and Sun Quan faced Cao Cao's huge force across the Yangtze. Zhou Yu, the brilliant commander of Wu, was jealous of Zhuge Liang, the strategist of his ally, and looked for a way to ruin him. He asked Zhuge Liang to produce one hundred thousand arrows for the coming battle within ten days.

To his surprise, Zhuge Liang said three days would be enough, and signed a pledge to accept punishment if he failed. He then asked Lu Su, a friendly officer, for twenty boats, each with a crew of soldiers, covered with cloth screens and lined with bundles of straw. For two days he did nothing at all.

On the third night a thick fog rolled over the river. Before dawn, Zhuge Liang had the boats tied together and rowed toward Cao Cao's camp, with the crews beating drums and shouting as if attacking. Cao Cao, unable to see anything in the fog and fearing a trap, ordered his archers to shoot rather than sail out. Arrows rained down on the straw. Zhuge Liang turned the boats to load the other side evenly.

As the fog lifted, the boats rowed away bristling with arrows, more than a hundred thousand of them. Zhuge Liang told the astonished Lu Su that he had read the weather three days before.
lesson: Know the conditions and your opponent's habits well enough, and you can make a rival's caution supply what you lack.
people: Zhuge Liang, Zhou Yu, Lu Su, Cao Cao
location: Yangtze River near Red Cliffs, China
source: Luo Guanzhong, Romance of the Three Kingdoms, Chapter 46
caveat: The episode is fiction; the historical records give no such feat to Zhuge Liang, though a similar tale is told of Sun Quan.
